text:
sasha: Quick follow-up to the on-prem/air-gapped packaging + upgrade RFC I posted yesterday. Wanted to capture open questions and proposed options here so we can lock the design before eng-sig next week.

ajay: Thanks — can you list the hard constraints again? air-gap means no outbound, ops must ship artifacts manually? :thinking:

sasha: Correct. No outbound by default. Ops will receive bundles (tar.gz or image archives) via secure transfer. We'll need signature verification and an offline verification flow. Also need transactional upgrades for stateful clusters.

jen: For package formats: prefer OCI image tarballs for runtime containers, and a signed metadata bundle for orchestration/config. Debian/RPM are painful in air-gapped envs.

kevin: +1 for OCI tarballs. How do we do deltas though? Large tar uploads every patch will be a pain for customers.

maria: We should design a delta patch format but fallback to full bundle. Also we need a documented rollback path — customers will ask for guaranteed revert within 5m.

ajay: Options I see:
- A) Full immutable bundles (tar of images + manifest + migrations), atomic swap by moving symlink and restarting services. Simple, robust, bigger uploads.
- B) Delta layers via binary diffs (bsdiff/rdiff) for images + layer dedupe. Smaller transfers, more complex apply logic and higher risk for corruption.
- C) Package manager + local repo mirror (apt/yum) shipped as mirror snapshot. Good for OS deps but doesn't solve runtime container images well.

sasha: Tradeoffs: A has lowest ops complexity, best for audit/compliance. B saves bandwidth but increases upgrade complexity and test surface. C fits customers who rely on system packages.

jen: For atomicity, what about a two-phase upgrade controller: upload -> preflight (verify sigs, run dry-run migrations) -> staged switch -> healthcheck -> commit. If healthcheck fails, auto-rollback to previous symlinked bundle.

kevin: Healthchecks must include DB migrations. We should support a migration dry-run mode that validates SQL but can be long. Maybe require a migration window for large schema changes.

maria: Also think about long-lived KV caches and local disk state. Rollback could need data compatibility checkers. We can't blindly restore files. Need a migration compatibility manifest per bundle.

sasha: Agreed. Proposal for RFC follow-up:
1) Default: Option A (immutable bundle) + manifest with required preflight checks + signed bundle (cosign).
2) Delta: optional feature for customers who opt-in and sign an SLA; we provide a delta tool that generates layer diffs.
3) Upgrade controller: two-phase with preflight, staged rollout, healthchecks, commit/rollback. Expose CLI and console.
4) Migration approach: migrations tagged with id + backwards-compatible flag. Non-backward migrations require explicit operator approval and scheduled maintenance window.

ajay: How do we do signature verification offline? We need a local trust store and rotation plan. If we use cosign, customers can upload a root public key into the vault and use it to verify bundles. Document key rollover steps.

jen: Example verify snippet for docs: 

```
# verify bundle signed with cosign
cosign verify-blob --key /etc/redwood/trust/root.pub --signature bundle.tar.gz.sig bundle.tar.gz
```

kevin: Nice. Also add SHA256 manifest entries and timestamped attestations for provenance. Customers will want an audit trail.

maria: Ops UX: CLI should allow "dry-run --apply-if-ok" and an "--offline-accept" flag for environments where a human will transfer the bundle and confirm signature. Needs clear prompts.

sasha: Question to infra/security: any objections to cosign + local trust store approach?

deploy-bot: Note: previous deploy policy requires signed images for hosted; we should align on tooling to reuse signing keys where possible.

ajay: No objections from infra but add HSM/KMS integration doc for enterprises who want private keys in HSM. Key rotation flow is critical.

jen: Testing: we need an airgap test harness that simulates no-outbound network and enforces operator bundle install via tar piped into the system. Add this to CI as an optional matrix.

kevin: For rollback speed, snapshot-based fs (LVM/zfs) or container overlay checkpointing could let us revert faster than re-extracting bundles. Add recommended storage options to docs.

maria: One more thing — telemetry. In air-gapped mode we can't phone-home. The agent should store anonymized telemetry to be pulled by ops and include an export command for support bundles.

sasha: Great feedback. Action items I propose:
- sasha: update RFC doc with default Option A, delta opt-in, 2-phase controller, cosign example, migration policy.
- ajay: draft key rotation & HSM integration notes.
- jen: prototype offline verification CLI flags + docs snippet.
- kevin: run a POC for LVM snapshot rollback and add perf numbers.
- maria: draft operator runbook for manual bundle transfer + support bundle export.

sasha: I'll push updates by EOW and tag this thread. If you have any blockers post them here. Thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin: Sounds good. I'll try the LVM POC tomorrow.

jen: I'll add the cosign snippet to the ops docs and mock the offline CLI UX.

maria: I'll sketch the runbook and include a checklist for maintenance windows.

ajay: I'll write the HSM flow and edge-case notes for delta patches.

sasha: tagging eng-ops folks to review later.

deploy-bot: Reminder: meeting scheduled 2024-05-10 16:00 UTC to finalize on-prem upgrades RFC.
